newsitem.title: USA: Silicon Graphics slashes Octane prices.
newsitem.headline: Silicon Graphics slashes Octane prices.

text.p: Silicon Graphics Inc said it is cutting the price of its Octane power desktop workstations by up to 20 percent while improving performance of its O2 entry-level desktop computers by up to 13 percent.

The announcements, to be made Tuesday at the SIGGRAPH 97 trade show in Las Vegas, are aimed at boosting demand for the workstations, a type of computer used for number crunching calculations ranging from movie effects to automated design.
Silicon Graphics, based in Mountain View, Calif., said all pricing and upgrades of its systems are effective immediately.

Silicon Graphics is expected to face rising competition in its core workstation market from increasingly powerful personal computer. But its machines still have performance advantages and it recently posted stronger than expected earnings boosted by sales of new models after a bumpy product transition.

Patrick Tickle, marketing manager for desktop workstations at Silicon Graphics, said market reception for the new desktop workstaitons had been "extremely favorable" and the price moves will enable more customers to gain access to the products.

The price reduction equates to a $5,000 cost savings on all Octane configurations, with a new entry point at $19,995, Silicon Graphics said. Prices for the workstation family range as high as $55,495, with systems equipped with dual processors starting at a U.S. list price of $28,495.

The O2 family consists of nine configurations priced from $5,995 to $15,495. The company said application performance increases on the O2 workstation are attributed to introduction of the 200 Megahertz MIPS RISC R5000 processor and an increase in L2 cache to 1 megabyte from 512 kilobytes.
